Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Clothes & getting dressed

suit verb

look good on someone; be fitting for

also become (look good on), look good on, it suits you, befit, be becoming

classical

Plaut. Most. 1.3.16: ut haec mē decet (Lewis & Short)
Prop. 4.4.53: tē toga picta decet (Lewis & Short)

decet, decēre, decuit

verb, second conjugation, impersonal: the thing as subject, the person in the accusative

it suits, becomes, befits

Of clothes, colours and looks as of conduct: what becomes a person. Its everyday sense is the moral one, “it is proper, one ought” (nōn decet, it isn’t done); Cicero defines it as what is apt to the time and the person (Or. 74, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • conveniō, convenīre, convēnī, conventum — fit, suit (a person, an age, an occasion)

    verb, fourth conjugation, intransitive: the thing as subject, the person in the dative; often impersonal, convenit · also used · classical · Mart. 14.47.1: mītis mihi convenit aetās · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: “it is fit, becoming, suitable”. The verb’s first sense is “come together, meet”; impersonally convenit is also “it is agreed”.

Examples

  • quīn mē aspice et contemplā, ut haec mē decet

    go on, look at me and see how well this suits mePlaut. Most. 1.3.16 (Lewis & Short)

  • parvum parva decent

    small things suit a small manHor. Ep. 1.7.44

  • īte procul, juvenēs: mītis mihi convenit aetās: folle decet puerōs lūdere, folle senēs

    off you go, young men: a gentle age suits me; it suits boys to play with the soft ball, and old men tooMart. 14.47.1–2

  • Hic color tē decet.

    This colour suits you.composed

See also suit, fit, suit.
